title: Serve many concurrent LLM requests
problem: A supported model and accelerator with real concurrency requirements.
rationale: Benchmark vLLM and SGLang as serving alternatives on your request mix; batching and cache reuse benefits depend on workload.
first_step: Deploy one server and a bounded load test before adding a cluster or custom scheduler.
validation: Record p50/p95 time to first token, inter-token latency, throughput, memory and cost at the same quality and context distribution.
caveat: Peak tokens per second can hide poor interactive latency; verify exact model, quantization and hardware support.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Prototype on Apple silicon
problem: A local Apple-silicon machine and a supported model.
rationale: Use MLX for local array/model experimentation, llama.cpp for supported quantized LLM execution, or Core ML for app deployment.
first_step: Choose one path based on research versus app distribution; do not convert through all three by default.
validation: Test end-to-end latency, sustained memory pressure, quality after conversion and deployment target compatibility.
caveat: Unified memory still has finite capacity; operator and format compatibility constrain model choice.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Put inference in a web browser
problem: Client-side processing can reduce server transfer and improve offline behavior.
rationale: Transformers.js is a task-model route; WebLLM is a chat-model route. Use WebGPU only where the browser and device support it.
first_step: Ship one small supported model and a clear download/progress indicator with a fallback for unsupported devices.
validation: Measure first-load download, warm latency, memory, battery impact and behavior across real target browsers.
caveat: Client-side execution exposes model assets and code; large downloads can outweigh hosting savings.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Evaluate an LLM before deployment
problem: A new model, prompt or system configuration needs a release gate.
rationale: Use Inspect AI for structured agent/model evaluations; promptfoo for prompt/API regression comparisons; pytest for deterministic application checks.
first_step: Create 30–100 representative cases with explicit scoring rubrics and failures from real usage.
validation: Separate deterministic checks, human review and model-graded scores; inspect disagreements and confidence intervals.
caveat: Benchmark success is not deployment safety; guard against contamination, judge bias and weak task coverage.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Study reward hacking or unsafe behavior
problem: Authorized research with bounded tasks and reproducible baselines.
rationale: Build controlled task families and use adversarial tooling to explore failures, rather than treating a red-team score as a safety certificate.
first_step: Use synthetic or authorized environments, immutable task definitions and a baseline model before increasing pressure.
validation: Compare task success with genuine objective success; manually audit outliers and measure false positives.
caveat: Preserve human oversight, permissions and a clear containment boundary; do not confuse capability failure with intentional deception.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested
